chapter: Arrangers, Bill Robinson and Coleman Hawkins
title: Bill Robinson, Ben Webster and ballads
summary: Thomas recalls playing Robinson's tune on flute, Bojangles dancing equally on both feet, Ben Webster's laughter, and Ben as a great ballad player.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: And another beautiful thing I did when I was playing the show... Benny Payne used to play that little thing for Bill Robinson... [SINGS REFRAIN] And I got an idea of doing it on flute. And that knocked Bill Robinson out. [BOTH SING IT] Man, he could dance.
Yeah. He was great to work with. He was bossy, but he was great.
He could dance. And anything he did on his right foot, he could do on his left.
And Ben Webster was his greatest fan. Ben Webster would laugh so loud at his jokes. [LOUD ROAR] He'd just fall out. And that would knock Bojangles out.
Yeah, Ben was his... And you know another thing Ben did, Ben... Although he didn't study, but Ben copied to play like us when we played the section.
Oh yes. He was very sensitive about that.
And I liked him, man. Because you see, what I discerned about Ben, Ben played a ballad as good as anybody I ever heard play saxophone.
I never heard anybody play a ballad better than Ben.
